limitations: These are provider-neutral deterministic rules, not a released runtime API or protocol-specific price adapter.
Consumers may impose stricter scale, zero, confidence, or numeric-range rules and must name them explicitly.

datumEnvelope.rawValue: signed base-10 integer or exact rational; never an unqualified floating-point number
datumEnvelope.scale: decimal exponent or decimals with explicit interpretation
datumEnvelope.confidence: source-defined raw value and semantics, or null with an unsupported limitation

scaling.multiplication: When sourceExponent + targetDecimals is non-negative, multiply exactly after checking the declared exponent and target numeric range.
scaling.division: When sourceExponent + targetDecimals is negative, divide by the exact power of ten and apply the named rounding rule; preserve whether a remainder was discarded.

confidence.rule: Normalize a feed-defined confidence integer with the same exponent and target scale as its paired raw price.
confidence.absent: Return null and a source limitation; never infer zero, a percentage, or an interval.
confidence.pairing: Confidence never survives without the exact source price, exponent, feed identity, and publication coordinate it qualifies.

invalidInputRule: An unavailable or invalid input is never converted to zero, a last-known value, or another source without an explicit typed result.
